evals.name: go-orders-isolation-and-dead-assertions
evals.expected_output: Catches the package-level testDB that makes TestSaveOrder_Duplicate depend on TestSaveOrder running first (P1), the error-only assertion in TestPlaceOrder, the fakeNotifier fields nothing reads, the vague TestHandler name, and CancelOrder's total absence of coverage — without claiming ApplyDiscount is uncovered, since TestPlaceOrder_AppliesVolumeDiscount flows through it.
assertions: Flags the package-level testDB shared via TestMain as an isolation defect, naming the order dependence between TestSaveOrder and TestSaveOrder_Duplicate
Rates the testDB order dependence P1 (it causes interference today, not merely a fragile-state hazard)
Flags TestPlaceOrder for asserting only that err is nil while never inspecting the returned Order
Flags the fakeNotifier recording reasons/lastID that no assertion ever reads (dead expectation)
Flags CancelOrder as exported production code with no test exercising it
Flags TestHandler as a name that does not communicate the scenario under test
Does NOT claim ApplyDiscount is uncovered — it is exercised transitively by TestPlaceOrder_AppliesVolumeDiscount
Reports no more than one P1 finding
Report follows REFERENCE.md: an 'N files reviewed, M issues found' header line and H3 findings tagged [P1]/[P2]/[P3] with a Location line
Every finding carries a concrete, file-readable 'done when' criterion
Total findings do not exceed 10

assertions: Flags `expect(mockFetch).toBeDefined()` in user.test.ts as a test that cannot fail, rated P1
Reports the module-scope globalThis.fetch replacement as ONE collapsed finding listing the affected files, not as a separate finding per file

Report follows REFERENCE.md: an 'N files reviewed, M issues found' header line and H3 findings tagged [P1]/[P2]/[P3] with a Location line
Every finding carries a concrete, file-readable 'done when' criterion

evals.name: py-clean-no-false-positives
evals.expected_output: Stays quiet. The suite parametrizes valid, invalid and boundary rates, asserts on returned values, tests both error branches, and shares only read-only reference data. Correct output is zero findings, or at most one P3.
assertions: Reports zero findings, or at most one finding and that finding is P3
Reports no P1 and no P2 findings
Does NOT flag the session-scoped known_rates fixture or the KNOWN_RATES constant as a shared mutable state hazard — both are read-only
Does NOT flag _round_half_up as a coverage gap above P3; it is internal and exercised through convert
Says plainly that the suite is sound rather than manufacturing findings to fill a report

evals.name: py-mixed-severity-and-cap
evals.expected_output: Separates real falsifiability defects (module-level _cache order dependence, the skipped refund test leaving refund unverified, an apply_tax assertion that reimplements the production formula, FakeTransport fields nothing asserts, test_1's name and non-assertion) from low-value noise, keeps severities anchored, and does not review the deliberately malformed testdata/ JSON.
assertions: Flags the module-level _cache making test_build_invoice_uses_cached_invoice_customer depend on a prior test, rated P1
Flags that refund's only test is skipped, leaving exported refund behaviour unverified
Flags test_apply_tax_accepts_valid_rates for asserting against `int(1000 * rate)`, which reimplements the production formula rather than pinning expected values
Flags FakeTransport recording last_subject/last_body that no assertion reads (dead expectation)
Flags test_1 for its uninformative name, its `assert inv is not None`, or both
Raises no finding against testdata/broken_invoice.json — it is deliberately malformed test input, not a test
If the time.sleep(1) test is flagged at all, it is rated no higher than P3
Reports no more than one P1 finding
Report follows REFERENCE.md: an 'N files reviewed, M issues found' header line and H3 findings tagged [P1]/[P2]/[P3] with a Location line
Total findings do not exceed 10, with a truncation footer if any were cut
